name: Air Quality Strategy framework for local authority delivery
fact: The strategy requires local authorities to assess air quality, declare AQMAs where objectives are exceeded or likely to be exceeded, and prepare Air Quality Action Plans; it also links planning decisions to relevant air-quality objectives and cumulative impacts.
gate: Planning impact remains proposal- and location-specific.

name: Local Air Quality Management statutory directions
fact: Secretary of State directions require specified English local authorities to conduct annual air-quality review or produce action plans under the Local Air Quality Management framework.
gate: Statutory process context is not parcel-specific evidence.

name: Planning Practice Guidance air quality
fact: Planning guidance says air quality can be a material consideration depending on the development and location, including baseline conditions, construction/operation effects, cumulative impacts and exposure of future users.
gate: A site-specific air-quality assessment may be required; guidance alone cannot score a parcel.

name: Defra Local Air Quality Management portal
fact: Defra's LAQM portal explains that local authorities periodically review current and future air quality and must designate an AQMA where objectives are not likely to be met.
gate: Use current local measurements and action plans for exact site evaluation.
